tonal_mismatches.line_excerpt: Simon thought it, not out loud: "This man, if he were a prophet..."
tonal_mismatches.rationale: Beat spans three distinct registers (Simon's cold unspoken judgment, Jesus's measured parable-telling, Simon's grudging reply) under one shared tag-set; acceptable under this project's one-tag-set-per-paragraph convention, but the tag captures the parable's cadence better than Simon's flatter opening and closing lines.

concerns: The <speaker name="jesus"> block on 'Which of them will love him most?' is a short, isolated dialogue turn; per-turn synthesis renders non-narrator turns at natural (untouched) speed, so confirm this short line doesn't sound clipped or abrupt in isolation.

Three separate quotes use mid-quote ellipses to mark elided KJV clauses; confirm ElevenLabs renders '...' as a clean join rather than an audible pause/trail-off, since a hesitation reading would misrepresent these as edited, not elided, text.

Paragraph 4 is the piece's one 3-tag rhetorical peak ([reflective][deliberate][emphasized]) per the tag-economy rule reserving 3 tags for a single peak beat; confirm on listen-back that '[emphasized]' lands on the forgiveness declaration and not inadvertently on the preceding narrator aside.
